name: Make It Grain Woodworks
old_description: Waterfall mitered joints, beveled edges, secret compartments, soft-close hinges, wireless charging…. You decide how deep we take the details.
about:
Make It Grain Woodworks operates from Boise, Idaho, producing hand-crafted furniture and premium cutting boards. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, but its website emphasizes a commitment to traditional woodworking methods and domestic materials.

The shop builds living-area, bedroom, and dining or conference tables, along with cutting boards, using kiln-dried hardwood selected board by board. Joinery includes mortise-and-tenon, half-lap, and screw fastening chosen per application. Finishes are applied after extensive prep work, and the shop integrates features such as waterfall mitered joints, beveled edges, secret compartments, soft-close hinges, and wireless charging pads. All work is described as custom, with clients involved in the design process.

Customers are primarily residential buyers seeking custom pieces, though conference tables suggest a commercial segment. The company positions itself against mass-produced imports that use engineered wood and low-wage overseas labor.

The stated differentiation rests on material quality, joinery variety, finish preparation, and collaborative design.
